title: Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
authors: Tilmann Gneiting; Adrian E. Raftery
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association 102(477):359–378
finding: Establishes proper scoring as a basis for eliciting and evaluating probability distributions.
caveat: Expected-score incentives do not eliminate finite-sample uncertainty.
vorhersage_implication: Define score conventions and retain forecast distributions.

title: Psychological Strategies for Winning a Geopolitical Forecasting Tournament
authors: Barbara Mellers et al.
finding: Probability training, collaboration, and tracking improved human forecasting.
caveat: Human intervention effects require separate validation for AI systems.
vorhersage_implication: Test training guidance, independent estimates, and collaboration.

title: Developing expert political judgment: The impact of training and practice on judgmental accuracy in geopolitical forecasting tournaments
authors: Welton Chang; Eva Chen; Barbara Mellers; Philip Tetlock
finding: Brief CHAMPS KNOW training improved human Brier scores by 6–11%.
caveat: Does not estimate an LLM treatment effect.
vorhersage_implication: Use forecasting principles as testable interventions.

title: ForecastQA: A Question Answering Challenge for Event Forecasting with Temporal Text Data
authors: Woojeong Jin et al.
finding: Introduces 10,392 forecasting questions using time-restricted news.
caveat: Multiple-choice accuracy differs from probabilistic event forecasting; versions report different baseline accuracy.
vorhersage_implication: Keep task type and publication version explicit.

title: Forecasting Future World Events with Neural Networks
authors: Andy Zou et al.
finding: Autocast links tournament questions to dated news; larger models and relevant retrieval improve results.
caveat: A fixed historical test becomes vulnerable as model training windows advance.
vorhersage_implication: Import question, evidence-date, and numeric-target metadata.

title: AutoCast++: Enhancing World Event Prediction with Zero-shot Ranking-based Context Retrieval
authors: Qi Yan; Raihan Seraj; Jiawei He; Lili Meng; Tristan Sylvain
finding: Relevance ranking, recency, and summarization improve retrieval-based event prediction.
caveat: Dataset-specific gains do not establish live generalization.
vorhersage_implication: Separate retrieval selection from probability synthesis.

title: Large Language Model Prediction Capabilities: Evidence from a Real-World Forecasting Tournament
authors: Philipp Schoenegger; Peter S. Park
finding: GPT-4 underperformed the human crowd and was not significantly different from a 50% baseline.
caveat: Applies to the tested early model and protocol.
vorhersage_implication: Preserve a simple prospective baseline.

title: Approaching Human-Level Forecasting with Language Models
authors: Danny Halawi; Fred Zhang; Yueh-Han Chen; Jacob Steinhardt
finding: Retrieval, reasoning, and aggregation approach competitive human-crowd performance.
caveat: Later methodological work identifies residual leakage risks; repeated forecast dates require careful weighting.
vorhersage_implication: Build modular research and aggregation baselines.

title: Wisdom of the Silicon Crowd: LLM Ensemble Prediction Capabilities Rival Human Crowd Accuracy
authors: Philipp Schoenegger; Indre Tuminauskaite; Peter S. Park; Rafael Valdece Sousa Bastos; Philip E. Tetlock
locator: Study 1 and Study 2 abstracts; published DOI 10.1126/sciadv.adp1528
finding: A twelve-model ensemble was not statistically different from a human crowd; combining human and AI predictions was useful.
caveat: Only 31 questions; failure to reject difference is not universal equivalence.
vorhersage_implication: Retain independent member forecasts and a simple aggregate.

title: Superhuman Automated Forecasting
authors: Center for AI Safety; accompanying report by Long Phan et al.
read_depth: Primary announcement; report itself not retrieved
finding: Announces the FiveThirtyNine forecasting system and crowd-level performance claims.
caveat: The announcement relies on cutoff and date-restricted search assumptions subsequently challenged.
vorhersage_implication: Retain as a historically influential claim, not decisive capability evidence.

title: ForecastBench: A Dynamic Benchmark of AI Forecasting Capabilities
authors: Ezra Karger; Houtan Bastani; Yueh-Han Chen; Zachary Jacobs; Danny Halawi; Fred Zhang; Philip E. Tetlock
evaluation_design: Prospective; mixed dataset and market questions
finding: The original human comparison favors superforecasters; evaluation combines multiple horizons and source categories.
caveat: Some unresolved market forecasts use crowd proxies; overall weighting differs from a pooled Brier mean.
vorhersage_implication: Store score target, horizon, and aggregation policy.

title: Consistency Checks for Language Model Forecasters
authors: Daniel Paleka; Abhimanyu Pallavi Sudhir; Alejandro Alvarez; Vineeth Bhat; Adam Shen; Evan Wang; Florian Tramèr
finding: Uses arbitrage on logically related forecasts as an immediate diagnostic and reports correlation with Brier performance.
caveat: Coherence alone cannot establish accurate beliefs.
vorhersage_implication: Add complement, conjunction, conditional, and horizon checks.

title: Pitfalls in Evaluating Language Model Forecasters
authors: Daniel Paleka; Shashwat Goel; Jonas Geiping; Florian Tramèr
finding: Identifies outcome-selection leakage, unreliable historical retrieval, cutoff uncertainty, copied crowd signals, and correlated tournament risk.
caveat: Some examples illustrate possible mechanisms rather than quantify every system's bias.
vorhersage_implication: Maintain multiple temporal controls and explicit comparison conditions.

title: MIRAI: Evaluating LLM Agents for Event Forecasting
authors: Chenchen Ye et al.
evaluation_design: Historical relational prediction with GDELT and news tools
finding: Provides an agent environment combining structured international events and textual evidence.
caveat: Relational prediction metrics are not interchangeable with tournament Brier scores.
vorhersage_implication: Support tools over structured event histories.

title: FOReCAst: The Future Outcome Reasoning and Confidence Assessment Benchmark
authors: Zhangdie Yuan; Zifeng Ding; Andreas Vlachos
finding: Covers Boolean outcomes, timeframes, and quantities with confidence assessment.
caveat: No numerical superiority claim extracted at this reading depth.
vorhersage_implication: Plan schemas beyond binary events.

title: FutureX: An Advanced Live Benchmark for LLM Agents in Future Prediction
authors: Zhiyuan Zeng et al.
finding: Introduces a live, frequently updated benchmark evaluating 25 LLM/agent systems.
caveat: Inspect task-specific scoring and sampling before comparing ranks with other platforms.
vorhersage_implication: Maintain an adapter for prospective evaluation.

title: Bench to the Future: A Pastcasting Benchmark for Forecasting Agents
authors: Jack Wildman; Nikos I. Bosse; Daniel Hnyk; Peter Mühlbacher; Finn Hambly; Jon Evans; Dan Schwarz; Lawrence Phillips
finding: Pairs resolved questions with offline web corpora for repeatable agent evaluation.
caveat: Training-cutoff validity changes with the model; availability is not equivalent to a fully open corpus.
vorhersage_implication: Version frozen evidence and model eligibility.

title: AIA Forecaster: Technical Report
authors: Rohan Alur; Bradly C. Stadie; Daniel Kang et al.
evaluation_design: Retrospective benchmarks plus 64 resolved live markets
finding: Combines search, synthesis, and calibration; reports expert-comparable benchmark scores and complementarity with market forecasts.
caveat: Live evidence is smaller; 1,750 open-market comparisons use market prices rather than resolved outcomes.
vorhersage_implication: Evaluate market-assisted and market-blind modes separately.

title: LLM-as-a-Prophet: Understanding Predictive Intelligence with Prophet Arena
authors: Qingchuan Yang; Simon Mahns; Sida Li; Anri Gu; Jibang Wu; Haifeng Xu
finding: Finds horizon-sensitive model/market comparisons and no significant gain from the tested reasoning scaffold.
caveat: Market-level records share events; gross-return comparisons do not establish net profitability.
vorhersage_implication: Record lead times and test scaffolds behaviorally.

title: Automating Forecasting Question Generation and Resolution for AI Evaluation
authors: Nikos I. Bosse; Peter Mühlbacher; Jack Wildman; Lawrence Phillips; Dan Schwarz
finding: Creates 1,499 questions; a human audit finds four resolution errors in 100 cases.
caveat: A low automated annulment rate is not proof of high resolution quality; §5.3 contains inconsistent counts.
vorhersage_implication: Treat resolution as an auditable process with disputes and corrections.

title: Evaluating Strategic Reasoning in Forecasting Agents
authors: Tom Liptay; Dan Schwarz; Rafael Poyiadzi; Jack Wildman; Nikos I. Bosse
finding: Combined system scores 0.119 versus 0.130 for Opus on a matched subset; rationale and case analyses identify potential reasoning gaps.
caveat: Possible benchmark overfitting; rationale format confounding; research comparison changes supplied evidence.
vorhersage_implication: Test review interventions and preserve evidence-linked intermediate forecasts.

title: Agentic Forecasting using Sequential Bayesian Updating of Linguistic Beliefs
authors: Kevin Murphy
finding: Structured belief updates, aggregation, and calibration improve results; removing belief state costs 5.1 Brier Index points in an ablation.
caveat: Retrospective and mostly one base model; headline cohort differs from expanded ablation cohort; some modes use market priors.
vorhersage_implication: Represent current belief, evidence, and open questions explicitly.

title: Outcome-based Reinforcement Learning to Predict the Future
authors: Benjamin Turtel; Danny Franklin; Kris Skotheim; Luke Hewitt; Philipp Schoenegger
venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research, November 2025
finding: Forecast-specific RL makes a compact model competitive with larger baselines while improving calibration.
caveat: Synthetic questions and historical outcomes require leakage and generalization audits; versions differ.
vorhersage_implication: Export proper-score training data only after evaluation integrity exists.

title: Future-as-Label: Scalable Supervision from Real-World Outcomes
authors: Benjamin Turtel; Paul Wilczewski; Danny Franklin; Kris Skothiem
finding: Uses temporally masked inputs and realized outcomes for forecasting supervision.
caveat: Masking supplied text cannot remove model memorization or resolution error; an OpenReview version has different model details.
vorhersage_implication: Keep predictor inputs and resolver evidence separate.

title: Reaching the frontier of AI forecasting with reinforcement learning
authors: Scott Jeen; Matthew Aitchison; Maximilian Anthony Hugh Clark; Toby Shevlane; Ben Day
read_depth: Paper abstract/introduction and author publication page
finding: RL on roughly 10,000 questions improves gpt-oss-120b to frontier-comparable performance in the reported test.
caveat: Workshop evidence; full temporal and model-selection audits remain necessary.
vorhersage_implication: Compare training against cheaper calibration and sampling baselines.

title: Diversity is the Strength of the AI Crowd
authors: Matthew Aitchison; Scott Jeen; Toby Shevlane; Ben Day
finding: Model diversity changes marginal ensemble value; individual rank does not determine contribution.
caveat: One tournament, up to three runs per model, and sample counts do not equal monetary cost.
vorhersage_implication: Track residual dependence and validate ensemble selection out of sample.

title: Aligning LLMs with Human Uncertainty: A Beta-Bernoulli Calibrator for LLM Forecasting
authors: Hui Dai; Ryan Teehan; Parsa Torabian; Mengye Ren
evaluation_design: Learned calibration using outcomes and human forecasts
finding: Learns a distribution over event likelihood from initial estimates and human/outcome supervision.
caveat: Depends on the human training signal and domain mix; does not model evidence updates.
vorhersage_implication: Preserve provenance for learned calibration and second-order uncertainty.

title: What LLM Forecasters Know but Don't Say: Probing Internal Representations for Calibration and Faithfulness
authors: Raphaël Sarfati; Pratyush Ranjan Tiwari; Siddharth Boppana; Christopher J. Earls; Srikar Varadaraj; Eric Ho
finding: Probes improve calibration in tested models; evidence interventions can change forecasts without corresponding rationale changes.
caveat: Recent model-specific evidence; activation access is needed for the probing method.
vorhersage_implication: Use input interventions to audit reasoning claims.

title: LLM-based Agents for Forecasting and Prediction: Methods, Training, Evaluation, and Applications
authors: Xiaogang Xu et al.
finding: Maps standalone, tool-augmented, and hybrid forecasting and emphasizes evaluation limitations.
caveat: Secondary synthesis; template journal metadata does not establish journal publication.
vorhersage_implication: Use as a discovery map and verify claims in original papers.

title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
authors: Abdul Fatir Ansari et al.
venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research, October 2024
finding: Trains transformer architectures on tokenized numerical series for transferable forecasting.
caveat: A numerical foundation model is distinct from a general text-reasoning agent.
vorhersage_implication: Treat specialist models as forecast providers and comparators.

title: Are Language Models Actually Useful for Time Series Forecasting?
authors: Mingtian Tan; Mike A. Merrill; Vinayak Gupta; Tim Althoff; Thomas Hartvigsen
finding: Removing or simplifying the LLM component often preserves or improves results in tested systems.
caveat: Does not refute all contextual or hybrid forecasting.
vorhersage_implication: Require a component-removal baseline for expensive designs.

title: Probabilistic weather forecasting with machine learning
authors: Ilan Price et al.
finding: Shows strong probabilistic weather performance from a specialized learned model.
caveat: Domain-specific data and targets do not establish general geopolitical skill.
vorhersage_implication: Route suitable questions to specialist distributions.

title: Chronos-2: From Univariate to Universal Forecasting
authors: Abdul Fatir Ansari et al.
finding: Extends pretrained forecasting to related series and covariates.
caveat: Selected adjacent coverage, not an exhaustive time-series comparison.
vorhersage_implication: Allow covariate-aware numerical adapters.

title: Context is Key: A Benchmark for Forecasting with Essential Textual Information
authors: Andrew R. Williams et al.
evaluation_design: Numerical series with essential textual context
finding: Constructs tasks requiring text and numbers together; its prompting baseline outperforms tested alternatives.
caveat: Purpose-built contextual tasks differ from ordinary univariate series.
vorhersage_implication: Test whether text adds information beyond the numeric baseline.

title: Hindcast: Replaying Prediction Markets to Evaluate LLM Forecasters
authors: Xiao Ye; Jacob Dineen; Evan Zhu; Shijie Lu; Kevin Song; Ben Zhou
finding: Tests retrieval with dated social evidence and contemporaneous market baselines; benefit depends on coverage.
caveat: Selection judges evidence against the resolved side, creating an outcome-conditioned sampling concern; archive controls do not certify model training cutoffs.
vorhersage_implication: Record evidence coverage and archive selection effects.

title: Agentic Time Machine as an Infrastructure for Future-Event Forecasting
authors: Jingyi Chai; Bingyang Zheng; Xiangrui Liu; Hao Lu; Zihang Zhou; Tianchen Wang; Kemeng Zhang; Siheng Chen
evaluation_design: Filtered historical web replay plus live comparison
finding: Combines a replay filter with planner/solver/aggregator forecasting and reports alignment with live rankings.
caveat: The 11 correlation points include repeated runs and related ensembles; filtered replay needs independent temporal and selection audits.
vorhersage_implication: Compare replay rankings with prospective performance.

title: AI-Augmented Predictions: LLM Assistants Improve Human Forecasting Accuracy
authors: Philipp Schoenegger; Peter S. Park; Ezra Karger; Sean Trott; Philip E. Tetlock
venue: ACM Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems 15(1), Article 4
evaluation_design: Preregistered prospective experiment; 991 participants; six questions
finding: Both frontier-model assistants improve human accuracy relative to a weaker-model control.
caveat: Few questions, outlier sensitivity, and a control differing in both model capability and forecasting support.
vorhersage_implication: Compare assisted forecasts against both human-only and model-only baselines.

title: The Wisdom of Deliberating AI Crowds: Does Deliberation Improve LLM-Based Forecasting?
authors: Paul Schneider; Amalie Schramm
evaluation_design: Historical evaluation; 202 binary questions; four conditions
finding: Diverse models with shared information improve log loss after deliberation; homogeneous groups do not benefit.
caveat: Conditional result across several scenarios; full statistical and temporal audit remains pending.
vorhersage_implication: Distinguish deliberation from averaging and preserve estimates before discussion.

title: The Strategic Foresight of LLMs: Evidence from a Fully Prospective Venture Tournament
authors: Felipe A. Csaszar; Aticus Peterson; Daniel Wilde
finding: Several LLMs outperform the studied human evaluators; ensembles and human–AI teams do not beat the best model.
caveat: Ranking differs from probability accuracy; comparisons share 30 ventures and one domain.
vorhersage_implication: Test collaboration against the strongest constituent and retain event-level sample counts.
